text:
lucas: Quick question for the group — we're finalizing the backpressure policy for per-key burst exhaustion. Do we lean hard into early-shed (fast 429) at the edge or admit into a short queue and return 503 on overload?
anya: tl;dr: 429 preserves client retry semantics and avoids long tail latency, but 503 better signals a server-side capacity problem. both have tradeoffs.
phil: +1 to 429 for public API. Most clients already implement exponential backoff on 429s. 503 encourages retries too but clients treat it as server flakiness.
sre_jordan: Important: we currently have per-key burst credits implemented. If we early-shed with 429, we need clear headers so SDKs and customers know when it's quota vs global overload.
maya: can we split signals? 429 for per-key quotas/exhaustion, 503 for infra overload (node OOM / global depletion). That maps to expected retry behavior.
lucas: agrees but UX ask from console/product: customers want to see how often they hit per-key bursts vs infra shedding. We need telemetry and dashboard slices.
vlad: telemetry-wise we should emit: metric.counter(request.shed.{reason}) with tags {org, key, route, reason=per_key|global|precheck}, histogram(queue_time_ms), and a sampled trace for shed events.
phil: also add headers: X-RW-Shed: "per_key" | "global" | "precheck" and X-RW-Queue-Time: ms. And a retry-after on 429 when possible.
anya: careful with Retry-After — many clients ignore it. But it's still useful for polite SDKs.
sre_jordan: From infra perspective, admitting into a short queue (e.g., 200ms max) buys time for bursts and is good for per-key smoothing. But it increases headroom required and can amplify tail latencies.
maya: If we do short queues, we should cap total queued requests per-worker and prefer early-shed for orgs already over commit. Eg: per-org reserved capacity > threshold -> allow brief queue; otherwise 429 immediately.
lucas: That aligns with routing policy idea: route-by-policy at edge: if org has dedicated capacity, allow buffering and graceful degrade; on shared capacity, do early shed.
phil: Implementation note: router currently has a Precheck phase that checks quotas and credits. Precheck returns 429 currently. If we change to admit-and-queue we need a second admission check at worker. Two-phase flow: precheck -> token minted -> enqueue -> worker consumes.
vlad: sketch of header flow: at precheck response include: X-RW-Admission: "admit|reject" and X-RW-Burst-Credits: n. If admitted and then evicted at worker, return 503 with X-RW-Shed: "worker_evicted".
anya: We should keep precheck fast and cheap. Any heavy decision should be avoided there. Precheck must not try to predict current queue length across all workers.
sre_jordan: Agreed. Use local worker queue state for eviction. Also add a sampling path: when we shed, ensure we capture full request metadata (route, prompt size, tokens) for postmortem.
maya: Console work: add a "Shed Events" card per org with breakdown by reason, rate per minute, and example traces. Also show per-route % of requests dropped.
lucas: UX: make the default console alert: ">5% shed_rate over 5m" and suggest tuning: raise reserved capacity, add batching, or reduce concurrency in client.
phil: For rollout: feature flag gated. Plan: 0.5% canary (internal orgs), then 5% of traffic for orgs with >10k qps, then full. Telemetry must be in place before 5%.
vlad: Alerting: add SLO for shed_rate (goal <0.2% for paid tiers). Also create burn rate alert for queue length growth.
anya: Need to update SDKs to surface X-RW-Shed and exponential-backoff policy. Could add helper that recognizes our headers and does jittered retry.
sre_jordan: Remember idempotency: some chat endpoints aren't idempotent. If we 429 early, SDKs can safely retry if idempotency key present; otherwise we should prefer queueing if the request is likely in-flight.
maya: Good point. Maybe prefer queueing for streaming/generative requests when no idempotency token, but that's harder to guarantee.
lucas: For now: rule-of-thumb — if request has Idempotency-Key or is embed/rerank (idempotent), early-shed is fine. For streaming gen without key, short-queue with best-effort processing.
phil: Can we add a console toggle per-route: "favor availability (early shed)" vs "favor completion (queue)"? Ops teams could flip per-route.
vlad: Yes. Route-level policy in config: {prefer_queue: bool, max_queue_ms: int, max_queue_depth: int}. We can expose this in the console and as API.
ancillary: deploy-bot: "deploy /routers v2 started canary for 0.5%"
lucas: Action items: 1) vlad: define metrics & headers doc (PR) 2) anya: update precheck logic doc with two-phase flow 3) maya: console mockups for shed card and route toggle 4) phil: SDK header handling + retry helper 5) sre_jordan: add eviction sampling path and alerts.
anya: I'll open the tickets and link here.
phil: I'll stub the SDK helper this week.
sre_jordan: I'll add Prometheus counters and a Grafana dashboard draft.
maya: I'll drop mocks in #design when ready.
lucas: thanks team. Let's reconvene after we have the PRs. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: "canary deployment complete — 0.5% routers on v2. monitor shed_rate and queue_time."
